Bulgogi (Marinated Grilled Beef)

25 min (+ 1 hr marinate)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Grilling the Marinated Beef

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Beef ribeye or sirloin, thinly sliced150g300g450g600g
Soy sauce30ml60ml90ml120ml
Sugar10g20g30g40g
Asian pear, grated20g40g60g80g
Garlic, minced1 clove2 cloves3 cloves4 cloves
Ginger, minced¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Sesame oil5ml10ml15ml20ml
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Scallion, cut into 2-inch pieces1234
Toasted sesame seeds½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp

Steps

  1. If the beef isn't pre-sliced, freeze it 20-30 minutes first so it firms up and slices paper-thin.
  2. Grate the Asian pear into a bowl — it adds sweetness and its enzymes gently tenderize the beef.
  3. Stir in the soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and black pepper until the sugar dissolves.
  4. Add the sliced beef and coat every piece in the marinade.
  5. Cover and marinate at least 1 hour in the fridge — overnight is even better.
  6. Heat a large pan or grill pan over medium-high with a little oil until shimmering.
  7. Add the sliced onion and cook 1 minute until just softened and translucent.
  8. Add the beef in a single layer (cook in batches if crowded) and sear 2-3 minutes without moving it.
  9. Flip and cook 1-2 minutes more, until every piece is deep brown with no pink left.
  10. Stir in the scallion pieces for the last 30 seconds, then serve over rice topped with sesame seeds.

Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)

25 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Simmering Kimchi & Pork

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Napa cabbage kimchi, chopped100g200g300g400g
Kimchi brine/juice30ml60ml90ml120ml
Pork belly, sliced (or Spam, cubed)60g120g180g240g
Tofu, cubed50g100g150g200g
Onion, sliced20g40g60g80g
Scallion, chopped1234
Gochugaru½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Gochujang½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Garlic, minced1 clove2 cloves3 cloves4 cloves
Water or anchovy stock200ml400ml600ml800ml
Sesame oil½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp

Steps

  1. Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the pork belly 2-3 minutes until the edges turn golden.
  2. Add the chopped kimchi and cook 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant instead of raw-smelling.
  3. Stir in the gochugaru and gochujang, coating the kimchi and pork.
  4. Pour in the water and kimchi brine, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
  5. Reduce to a simmer, cover with the lid slightly ajar, and cook 10 minutes.
  6. Add the onion and garlic, and simmer 3 more minutes until the onion softens.
  7. Gently slide in the tofu cubes and simmer 2 more minutes, stirring carefully.
  8. Taste and add a splash more kimchi brine if it needs more depth.
  9. Turn off the heat, sprinkle scallion on top, and serve bubbling hot with rice.

Japchae (Glass Noodle Stir-Fry)

35 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Stir-Frying Noodles & Vegetables

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Sweet potato glass noodles (dangmyeon)50g100g150g200g
Beef sirloin, thin strips40g80g120g160g
Spinach40g80g120g160g
Carrot, julienned20g40g60g80g
Onion, sliced20g40g60g80g
Shiitake mushrooms, sliced15g30g45g60g
Soy sauce20ml40ml60ml80ml
Sugar10g20g30g40g
Sesame oil10ml20ml30ml40ml
Garlic, minced1 clove2 cloves3 cloves4 cloves
Toasted sesame seeds½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp

Steps

  1. Boil the glass noodles 6-8 minutes until soft, stretchy, and translucent, then drain and rinse with cold water.
  2. Snip the noodles a few times with kitchen scissors so they're easier to eat.
  3. Mix the soy sauce and sugar together, toss two-thirds of it with the noodles and 1 tsp sesame oil, and set aside.
  4. Sear the beef strips in a hot pan 2-3 minutes until no pink remains, then set aside.
  5. In the same pan, cook the onion, carrot, and shiitake 3-4 minutes until the carrot still has a little crunch.
  6. Add the spinach and stir just until wilted, about 1 minute.
  7. Return the beef and noodles to the pan with the rest of the soy-sugar mix, tossing 1-2 minutes until golden.
  8. Off heat, drizzle in the remaining sesame oil and toss once more.
  9. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

Doenjang Jjigae (Soybean Paste Stew)

25 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Dissolving the Doenjang Paste

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Doenjang15g30g45g60g
Zucchini, diced30g60g90g120g
Potato, diced30g60g90g120g
Onion, diced20g40g60g80g
Tofu, cubed50g100g150g200g
Garlic, minced½ clove1 clove1½ cloves2 cloves
Green chili, sliced¼½¾1
Scallion, chopped¼½¾1
Water or anchovy-kelp stock200ml400ml600ml800ml
Gochugaru (optional)pinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp

Steps

  1. Bring the water or stock to a boil in a small pot over medium-high heat.
  2. Stir in the doenjang until fully dissolved with no lumps.
  3. Add the diced potato first, since it takes longest, and simmer 5 minutes.
  4. Add the onion and zucchini, and simmer another 5 minutes until the potato is fork-tender.
  5. Stir in the garlic and optional gochugaru.
  6. Add the sliced green chili and simmer 2 more minutes.
  7. Gently add the tofu cubes and simmer 2 more minutes, stirring softly.
  8. Taste — it should be savory and earthy. Stir in a little more doenjang if it tastes flat.
  9. Turn off the heat, sprinkle scallion on top, and serve bubbling hot with rice.

Dakgalbi (Spicy Stir-Fried Chicken)

35 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Cooking Chicken & Vegetables in the Pan

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thigh, bite-size pieces150g300g450g600g
Gochujang15g30g45g60g
Gochugaru½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Soy sauce10ml20ml30ml40ml
Sugar5g10g15g20g
Garlic, minced1 clove2 cloves3 cloves4 cloves
Ginger, minced¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Green cabbage, chopped50g100g150g200g
Sweet potato, sliced30g60g90g120g
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Scallion, cut into pieces¼½¾1
Sesame oil½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp

Steps

  1. Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and ginger into a thick red sauce.
  2. Toss the chicken pieces in the sauce and marinate at least 15 minutes, up to an hour.
  3. Heat the sesame oil in a large wide pan over medium heat and cook the sweet potato 3-4 minutes first.
  4. Add the marinated chicken, spreading it out, and let it sear 3 minutes before flipping.
  5. Add the onion and cabbage, and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is fully cooked through.
  6. If it looks dry before the chicken is done, add a small splash of water.
  7. Stir in the scallion pieces in the last minute of cooking.
  8. Serve straight from the pan, family-style, with rice on the side.

Yangnyeom Chicken (Korean Fried Chicken)

45 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Double-Frying the Chicken

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken wings/drumettes200g400g600g800g
Cornstarch or potato starch30g60g90g120g
All-purpose flour15g30g45g60g
Saltpinch¼ tsp¼ tsp½ tsp
Neutral oil, for fryingas neededas neededas neededas needed
Gochujang15g30g45g60g
Ketchup15g30g45g60g
Honey or corn syrup10g20g30g40g
Soy sauce5ml10ml15ml20ml
Garlic, minced1 clove2 cloves3 cloves4 cloves
Toasted sesame seeds½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp

Steps

  1. Pat the chicken wings completely dry, then toss with salt and pepper.
  2. Coat every piece evenly in the cornstarch and flour mix, shaking off the excess.
  3. Heat about 2 inches of oil to 340°F/170°C in a deep, heavy pot.
  4. Fry the chicken in batches 7-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until light golden and cooked through.
  5. Drain on a wire rack and let the oil come back up to temperature.
  6. Fry all the pieces a second time for 2-3 minutes until deep golden brown and very crunchy.
  7. While the chicken drains, simmer the gochujang, ketchup, honey, soy sauce, and garlic in a pan 1-2 minutes until glossy.
  8. Toss the crispy chicken in the sauce off heat until every piece is coated.
  9. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve immediately while hot and crispy.

Bibimbap (Mixed Rice Bowl)

35 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Frying the Egg

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Cooked short-grain rice150g300g450g600g
Beef, ground or thin strips50g100g150g200g
Spinach30g60g90g120g
Carrot, julienned20g40g60g80g
Zucchini, julienned30g60g90g120g
Bean sprouts30g60g90g120g
Shiitake mushrooms, sliced15g30g45g60g
Egg1234
Gochujang15g30g45g60g
Sesame oil1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Garlic, minced1 clove2 cloves3 cloves4 cloves

Steps

  1. Boil the bean sprouts 2-3 minutes until just tender, then scoop out, keeping the water boiling.
  2. Boil the spinach 30 seconds, drain, rinse with cold water, and squeeze out excess water.
  3. Toss the bean sprouts and spinach separately with a pinch of salt, garlic, and sesame oil.
  4. Cook the carrot, zucchini, and shiitake separately, 1-2 minutes each, keeping their colors distinct.
  5. Cook the beef with a splash of soy sauce and garlic 3-4 minutes until fully browned.
  6. Fry the egg sunny-side up until the white sets but the yolk stays runny, about 3 minutes.
  7. Scoop warm rice into each bowl as the base.
  8. Arrange the toppings in separate piles around the rice like a clock face.
  9. Place the fried egg in the center with a spoonful of gochujang beside it.
  10. Drizzle with extra sesame oil and mix everything together just before eating.

Hotteok (Sweet Filled Pancakes, Bonus)

25 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Filling the Dough

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
All-purpose flour60g120g180g240g
Glutinous (sweet) rice flour15g30g45g60g
Sugar (for dough)5g10g15g20g
Instant yeast¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Warm milk or water45ml90ml135ml180ml
Brown sugar (filling)20g40g60g80g
Cinnamon¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Chopped peanuts or walnuts10g20g30g40g
Oil, for pan-fryingas neededas neededas neededas needed

Steps

  1. Stir the warm milk with sugar and yeast, and let it sit 5 minutes until foamy.
  2. Mix in the flour, glutinous rice flour, and salt to form a soft, sticky dough.
  3. Cover and let it rise somewhere warm 45-60 minutes until puffy and doubled.
  4. Mix the brown sugar, cinnamon, and chopped nuts for the filling.
  5. With oiled hands, flatten a golf-ball-size piece of dough in your palm.
  6. Add a spoonful of filling, gather the edges up, and pinch to seal the pouch.
  7. Heat oil in a flat pan over medium heat and place the pouch seam-side down for 1 minute.
  8. Press firmly to flatten into a thick disc, then cook 2-3 minutes until deep golden brown.
  9. Flip and press again lightly, cooking 2-3 minutes more until both sides are golden.
  10. Let it rest 1-2 minutes before serving warm — the filling stays molten hot inside.
